title: Preserve-Then-Quantize: Balancing Rank Budgets for Quantization Error Reconstruction in LLMs
claim: Quantizing the whole matrix leaves unrecoverable error; preserving dominant structure first and quantizing only the residual leaves far smaller error.
layout: 2 stacked rows, left-to-right flow, shared log-scale error colorbar on right
description: The figure compares two processing paths for a weight matrix, both drawn as green heatmaps. At top left is the Original Weight. A dashed arrow labeled Quantize leads into a gray QER box, first to a dark-green Quantization Error heatmap. A second dashed arrow labeled Low-rank Reconstruct leads to a Reconstruction Error heatmap that is still mid-green. Below, a solid black arrow splits the original weight under the blue word Preserve. One branch goes to a striped Preserved Directions heatmap. The other goes to a pale Residual heatmap inside a gray SRR box. Solid arrows then run through Then, Quantize (blue) and Low-rank Reconstruct. The resulting error maps are nearly pale yellow. A log-scale colorbar from 10^0 to 10^-5 sits on the right. The eye goes first to the color contrast between the dark top row and the pale bottom row.
caption: Preserve-then-quantize mechanism in Structured Residual Reconstruction (SRR), compared with standard QER. Top: In QER, quantizing the entire weight matrix destroys the intrinsic low-rank structure of the original weight, leaving errors that cannot be recovered by low-rank reconstruction. Bottom: In contrast, SRR preserves the dominant low-rank structure prior to quantization, preventing structural damage and resulting in a substantially smaller reconstruction error $\lVert \bW - \bQ - \bL\bR \rVert_F$ under the same rank budget.
abstract: Quantization Error Reconstruction (QER) reduces accuracy loss in Post-Training Quantization (PTQ) by approximating weights as $\mathbf{W} \approx \mathbf{Q} + \mathbf{L}\mathbf{R}$, using a rank-$r$ correction to reconstruct quantization error. Prior methods devote the full rank budget to error reconstruction, which is suboptimal when $\mathbf{W}$ has intrinsic low-rank structure and quantization corrupts dominant directions. We propose Structured Residual Reconstruction (SRR), a rank-allocation framework that preserves the top-$k$ singular subspace of the activation-scaled weight before quantization, quantizes only the residual, and uses the remaining rank $r-k$ for error reconstruction. We derive a theory-guided criterion for selecting $k$ by balancing quantization-exposed energy and unrecoverable error under rank constraints. We further show that resulting $\mathbf{Q} + \mathbf{L}\mathbf{R}$ parameterization naturally supports Quantized Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (QPEFT), and stabilizes fine-tuning via gradient scaling along preserved directions. Experiments demonstrate consistent perplexity reductions across diverse models and quantization settings in PTQ, along with a 5.9 percentage-point average gain on GLUE under 2-bit QPEFT. The project page is available at https://ai-isl.github.io/srr.
